questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The minister's speech was full of PLATITUDES.
questions.explanation: A platitude is a trite, overused remark presented as if it were novel or profound.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: Her CANDID assessment surprised the board.
questions.explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward, without evasion.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The old bridge was considered OBSOLETE.
questions.explanation: Obsolete describes something outdated and no longer used.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The witness gave a LUCID account of the accident.
questions.explanation: Lucid means expressed clearly, easy to follow.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: His ARROGANT manner offended many guests.
questions.explanation: Arrogant describes someone who has an exaggerated sense of their own importance.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The company's profits showed a GRADUAL increase.
questions.explanation: Gradual means taking place in small stages over a period of time.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: She remained IMPASSIVE despite the bad news.
questions.explanation: Impassive means not displaying or affected by emotion.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The professor's argument was quite COGENT.
questions.explanation: Cogent describes a clear, logical, and convincing argument.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The negotiations reached an AMICABLE settlement.
questions.explanation: Amicable means characterised by friendliness and absence of discord.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: He is known for his FRUGAL lifestyle.
questions.explanation: Frugal means careful with money or resources, avoiding waste.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The manager's decision was ARBITRARY.
options: Based on random whim rather than reason
questions.explanation: Arbitrary means based on random choice rather than any system or reason.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The evidence against him was IRREFUTABLE.
questions.explanation: Irrefutable means impossible to deny or disprove.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: Her explanation was rather TERSE.
questions.explanation: Terse means using few words; concise, sometimes curt.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The committee's report was highly CONTENTIOUS.
questions.explanation: Contentious means causing or likely to cause an argument.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The athlete showed great TENACITY throughout the race.
questions.explanation: Tenacity means the quality of being determined and not giving up.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: The instructions were extremely AMBIGUOUS.
questions.explanation: Ambiguous means open to more than one interpretation; its opposite is clear/unambiguous.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: The soldiers showed remarkable BRAVERY.
questions.explanation: Bravery is courage; its opposite is cowardice.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: The company's growth has been quite RAPID.
questions.explanation: Rapid means fast; the opposite is slow or sluggish.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: His response was surprisingly GENEROUS.
questions.explanation: Generous means willing to give; the opposite is stingy or miserly.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: The lecture hall was completely SILENT.
questions.explanation: Silent means making no sound; its opposite is noisy.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: The new policy is considered quite LENIENT.
questions.explanation: Lenient means permissive or not strict; the opposite is strict/harsh.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: The manager praised her PUNCTUALITY.
questions.explanation: Punctuality means being on time; the opposite is lateness/tardiness.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: The old man was known for his HUMILITY.
questions.explanation: Humility is modesty about one's importance; the opposite is arrogance/pride.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: The findings of the study were CONCLUSIVE.
questions.explanation: Conclusive means decisive/final; the opposite is inconclusive or uncertain.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word: The negotiations were marked by HOSTILITY.
questions.explanation: Hostility means unfriendliness or antagonism; the opposite is friendliness.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Fill the gap with the most suitable word: Despite his wealth, he lived a very ______ life, avoiding waste.
questions.explanation: Frugal fits the context of avoiding waste despite having wealth.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Fill the gap with the most suitable word: The manager's ______ attitude discouraged new ideas from the team.
questions.explanation: Dismissive fits the context of discouraging new ideas.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Fill the gap with the most suitable word: The government has promised to ______ the ailing power sector.
questions.explanation: Revamp means to improve or renovate, fitting the promise to fix the sector.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Fill the gap with the most suitable word: Her ______ remarks during the meeting embarrassed her colleagues.
questions.explanation: Tactless fits remarks that cause embarrassment.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Fill the gap with the most suitable word: The committee will ______ the proposal before the next session.
questions.explanation: Scrutinise means to examine closely, fitting review of a proposal.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Fill the gap with the most suitable word: The students were asked to ______ their findings in a short report.
questions.explanation: Summarise fits presenting findings concisely in a report.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Fill the gap with the most suitable word: The new regulation aims to ______ corrupt practices in public offices.
questions.explanation: Curb means to restrain or control, fitting a regulation against corruption.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Fill the gap with the most suitable word: The athlete's ______ performance earned her a gold medal.
questions.explanation: Outstanding fits a performance strong enough to win gold.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Fill the gap with the most suitable word: The lawyer presented ______ evidence that convinced the jury.
questions.explanation: Compelling fits evidence strong enough to convince a jury.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Fill the gap with the most suitable word: The professor's lecture was so ______ that many students fell asleep.
questions.explanation: Monotonous fits a lecture boring enough to put students to sleep.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Neither the students nor the teacher ______ aware of the change.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'the teacher' (singular).

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Each of the candidates ______ given ten minutes to speak.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes a singular verb 'was'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: By the time the rain started, we ______ the match.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had finished' shows an action completed before another past action.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If I ______ you, I would apologise immediately.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive mood uses 'were' for hypothetical situations after 'if I'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The report, along with the appendices, ______ due tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'the report' (singular); phrases like 'along with' do not change the verb agreement.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She is one of the students who ______ always punctual.
questions.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'students' (plural), so the verb should be 'are'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: He suggested that she ______ the report before submission.
questions.explanation: After 'suggest that', the subjunctive base form 'review' is used regardless of subject.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The number of applicants ______ increased significantly this year.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb; 'a number of' would take a plural verb.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Hardly ______ the meeting begun when the power went off.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly had' followed by 'when' is the correct inverted structure for past perfect.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Not only ______ the exam but she also scored the highest mark.
questions.explanation: 'Not only' at the start of a clause requires subject-auxiliary inversion.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: 'The classroom was a zoo during the break.'
questions.explanation: A metaphor directly states one thing IS another, without using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: 'Her smile was as bright as the morning sun.'
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using 'as' or 'like'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: 'The wind whispered through the trees.'
questions.explanation: Personification gives human qualities (whispering) to non-human things (wind).

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: 'I have told you a million times to stop that.'
questions.explanation: Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration for emphasis, not meant literally.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: 'Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.'
questions.explanation: Alliteration is the repetition of the same initial consonant sound in nearby words.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: 'The bomb exploded with a loud bang.'
questions.explanation: Onomatopoeia is a word that imitates the sound it describes, like 'bang'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: 'A jumbo shrimp is a common menu item.'
questions.explanation: An oxymoron combines two contradictory terms, like 'jumbo' and 'shrimp'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: 'It is an open secret that he plans to resign.'
questions.explanation: 'Open secret' combines two contradictory ideas, making it an oxymoron.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: 'The traffic crawled through the city centre.'
questions.explanation: Traffic 'crawling' gives it a human/animal action, a form of personification.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the figure of speech: Saying 'What a lovely day' during a heavy downpour.
questions.explanation: Irony involves saying the opposite of what is actually meant or true.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the proverb/idiom: 'A stitch in time saves nine.'
options: Acting early prevents bigger problems later
questions.explanation: This proverb emphasises the value of timely action to avoid larger issues.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'To let the cat out of the bag.'
questions.explanation: This idiom means to accidentally disclose confidential information.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'To bite the bullet.'
options: To face a difficult situation bravely
questions.explanation: This idiom means to endure a painful or difficult situation with courage.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'Once in a blue moon.'
questions.explanation: This idiom describes something that happens very infrequently.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'To beat around the bush.'
options: To avoid getting to the point directly
questions.explanation: This idiom means to speak evasively rather than addressing the main issue.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'To cost an arm and a leg.'
questions.explanation: This idiom describes something that is extremely costly.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'To be on the same page.'
options: To agree or have the same understanding
To work in the same office
questions.explanation: This idiom means people share the same views or understanding of a situation.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the proverb: 'Look before you leap.'
questions.explanation: This proverb advises careful consideration before taking action.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the idiom: 'To spill the beans.'
questions.explanation: This idiom means to disclose secret or private information.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the proverb: 'Every cloud has a silver lining.'
options: There is something good in every bad situation
Silver is more valuable than gold
questions.explanation: This proverb means that even difficult situations have a positive aspect.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following words has a silent letter?
questions.explanation: In 'knight', the letters 'k' and 'gh' are silent.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of these words contains a silent letter?
questions.explanation: In 'comb', the letter 'b' is silent.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the word below that has a silent letter.
questions.explanation: In 'doubt', the letter 'b' is silent.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the underlined syllables carries the primary stress in the word 'photograph'?
questions.explanation: In 'photograph', the primary stress falls on the first syllable.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the underlined syllables carries the primary stress in the word 'economics'?
questions.explanation: In 'economics', the primary stress falls on the third syllable.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which word rhymes with 'though'?
questions.explanation: 'Though' and 'toe' share the same 'oh' vowel sound despite different spellings.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which pair of words has the same vowel sound?
questions.explanation: 'Meat' and 'meet' are both pronounced with the long 'ee' sound.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which word contains a diphthong?
questions.explanation: The vowel sound in 'boy' (oi) is a diphthong, a glide between two vowel sounds.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of these words is stressed on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: 'Begin' carries its primary stress on the second syllable.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which word does NOT rhyme with the others?
questions.explanation: 'Beak' has a different vowel sound ('ee') from 'cake', 'lake', and 'break' which share the 'ay' sound.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Read the passage: 'Renewable energy sources like solar and wind are gaining popularity in Nigeria due to unreliable grid power. Many households now install solar panels as a backup, despite the initial cost being high for average earners. Advocates argue that widespread adoption could reduce dependence on fossil fuels and cut long-term electricity costs.' What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Solar panels are too expensive for anyone to afford
Nigeria has abandoned fossil fuels completely
Renewable energy is becoming popular as an alternative to unreliable grid power
Wind energy is more popular than solar energy
questions.explanation: The passage centres on renewable energy's growing popularity due to unreliable grid power.

questions.explanation: In this context, 'advocates' refers to people who support or promote renewable energy adoption.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Read the passage: 'Reading habits among young people have shifted dramatically with the rise of digital media. While some educators worry that screens are replacing books, others point out that e-books and audiobooks have made reading more accessible than ever, especially for those with limited access to physical libraries.' What concern do some educators express?
questions.explanation: The passage states some educators worry that screens are replacing traditional books.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Read the passage: 'Reading habits among young people have shifted dramatically with the rise of digital media. While some educators worry that screens are replacing books, others point out that e-books and audiobooks have made reading more accessible than ever, especially for those with limited access to physical libraries.' According to the passage, what benefit do e-books and audiobooks provide?
options: They are more expensive than physical books
They have completely replaced physical libraries
They are only used by educators
They have made reading more accessible, especially for those with limited library access

The passage suggests that opinions on digital media's effect on reading are:
questions.explanation: The passage presents both a worried perspective and an optimistic one, showing divided opinions.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Read the passage: 'Reading habits among young people have shifted dramatically with the rise of digital media. The word 'dramatically' in the passage is closest in meaning to:

Why Audiobooks Are Better Than Books
Digital Media and Changing Reading Habits

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: 'It's' is the contraction of 'it is', which is needed here.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of the following sentences is correctly punctuated?
options: The teachers book was on the desk.
The teachers' book was on the desk.
The teacher's book was on the desk.
The teachers books was on the desk.
questions.explanation: The apostrophe before 's' shows singular possession by one teacher.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Select the sentence with correct punctuation.
options: We bought, apples, oranges and bananas.
We bought apples, oranges, and bananas.
We bought apples oranges, and bananas.
We bought apples oranges and bananas.
questions.explanation: Commas are needed to separate items in a list.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option with the correctly spelled word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling follows 'i before e except after c': receive.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which of these words is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Necessary' has one 'c' and two 's's.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Identify the correctly spelled word below.
questions.explanation: 'Occasion' has two 'c's and one 's'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Select the option that is spelled correctly.
questions.explanation: 'Definitely' is derived from 'definite', not 'definate'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Which spelling below is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Embarrass' has a double 'r' and double 's'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the word that is spelled correctly.
questions.explanation: 'Accommodate' has a double 'c' and double 'm'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Pick the correctly spelled word from the options below.
questions.explanation: 'Privilege' has no 'd' and only one 'l'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She is good ______ mathematics but weak ______ physics.
questions.explanation: 'Good at' and 'weak in' are the standard prepositional collocations here.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The children were responsible ______ cleaning the compound.
questions.explanation: 'Responsible for' is the correct preposition to indicate a duty or task.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: He apologised ______ his colleague ______ the delay.
questions.explanation: One apologises 'to' a person 'for' an offence — the standard preposition pairing.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word: The politician's promises were largely SPECIOUS.
questions.explanation: Specious means seeming reasonable or true, but actually being wrong or misleading.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The committee members could not agree ______ the proposed budget.
questions.explanation: 'Agree on' is the correct preposition when referring to reaching consensus about a matter.
